panel.summary: `undoFloor` is an absolute stack depth compared against a Yorkie stack that can shrink independently (cap eviction / snapshot reset), so undo can silently stop early
panel.evidence: `canUndo()` requires `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor` with `undoFloor` frozen at construction (line 49). That is only sound if the stack never loses entries below the floor. In a text editor one CodeMirror transaction = one Yorkie change (per this PR's own design), so the stack grows one entry per keystroke and will hit Yorkie's stack bound; likewise a snapshot applied mid-session can reset it. Once the entries the floor was counting are gone, the comparison no longer means "above the seed" — it just refuses the user's oldest `undoFloor` genuine edits (or, after a reset, blocks undo entirely until the depth climbs back past the floor). A floor recorded as an identity/marker of the seed change rather than a raw depth would not have this failure mode. Same shape exists in the slides/docs/board stores, so this is a pattern-level risk, not one this PR invented — but it is newly load-bearing here because notes push far more undo units than those stores.
panel.finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts::`undofloor` is an absolute stack depth compared against a yorkie stack that can shrink independently (cap eviction / snapshot reset), so undo can silently stop early

coderabbit.detail: **Avoid depending on `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` outside tests.** `Document.getUndoStackForTest()` is exposed in `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13, but its `ForTest` suffix indicates it is a test helper, not the stable public history API. Keeping the store’s `undoFloor` calculation tied to this helper makes application code brittle to future SDK changes.
